agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: I used Claude Code and Codex for the translation. This was human-directed, not autonomous code generation.

also.quote: The /btw command is amazing for this! Lets you poke your head in whenever you want without sidetracking the main thread 😄
I asked Claude to write a bunch of tests to get proper coverage of our core JS engine optimizations, and this exposed two issues which are fixed herein.

review_style.value: Adversarial review passes by different models
review_style.quote: After the initial translation, I ran multiple passes of adversarial review, asking different models to analyze the code for mistakes and bad patterns.

also.quote:
Bargaining:
- Okay, AI can write code, but only if a human reviews every line.
- Maybe adversarial AI review will make arbitrary external code intake safe again.
(This was roughly my own thought process over the last ~12 months. Your journey may be different!)

Beyond the test suites, I’ve done extensive testing by browsing the web in a lockstep mode where both the C++ and Rust pipelines run simultaneously, verifying that output is identical for every piece of JavaScript that flows through them.

signature.caption: on workers across 4 machines
signature.why: Our pick: the coordinator, not he, watches for stuck or crash-looping workers, so multi-day runs need no steering.
signature.quote: 4. Tell coordinator to do regular welfare checks on all workers in case someone gets stuck/crash-loops/etc.

archetype.why: Writes the design doc, then lets a coordinator agent run workers on four machines for days.

signature_quote.value: I don't really steer. I just check in every now and then to see how things are going.
